abstract.p: Sentiment analysis in code-mixed languages, particularly Tamil-English, is a growing challenge in natural language processing (NLP) due to the prevalence of multilingual communities on social media. This paper explores various machine learning and transformer-based models, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), BERT, and mBERT, for sentiment classification of Tamil-English codemixed text. The models are evaluated on a shared task dataset provided by Dravidian-LangTech@NAACL 2025, with performance measured through accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Our results demonstrate that transformer-based models, particularly mBERT, outperform traditional classifiers in identifying sentiment polarity. Future work aims to address the challenges posed by codeswitching and class imbalance through advanced model architectures and data augmentation techniques.
